# US-01.3 — Install every dependency from one manifest

|                  |                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Epic**         | [EPIC-01 Foundation & Environment](../epics/EPIC-01-foundation-environment.md) |
| **Priority**     | P1                                                                             |
| **Estimate**     | 1                                                                              |
| **Status**       | Done                                                                           |
| **Owning agent** | `story-builder`                                                                |
| **Files**        | [requirements.txt](../../../requirements.txt)                                  |

## User story

**As a** developer or CI runner,
**I want** one manifest that installs the backend, frontend, and test dependencies,
**so that** `pip install -r requirements.txt` is the only setup step I ever need to remember.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Backend runtime**
Given a fresh virtual environment,
when I install the manifest,
then `google-genai`, the Firestore, Pub/Sub, BigQuery and Storage clients, `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `pydantic`, `pillow`, and `python-dotenv` are importable.

**AC2 — Frontend runtime**
Then `streamlit` and `requests` are importable, so [EPIC-07](../epics/EPIC-07-dashboard.md) can run without a second manifest.

**AC3 — Test tooling**
Then `pytest`, `pytest-cov`, and `httpx` are importable, so [EPIC-08](../epics/EPIC-08-quality-assurance.md) can measure coverage and drive `TestClient`.

**AC4 — Clean install**
Given an empty venv on Python 3.10 or newer,
when I run `pip install -r requirements.txt`,
then it completes with no dependency conflicts.

**AC5 — Single source of truth**
Given a new third-party package is needed,
then it is added here — not installed ad hoc, and not duplicated in a second requirements file.

## Tasks

- [x] Pin minimum versions with `>=` rather than exact pins, so the hackathon build picks up fixes
- [x] Add the frontend dependencies `streamlit` and `requests`
- [x] Add the test dependencies `pytest`, `pytest-cov`, `httpx`
- [x] Verify a clean install into a fresh venv

## Current state

Complete. The manifest carries all three groups in one file:

| Group    | Packages                                                                                                                                   |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Backend  | google-cloud-aiplatform, google-genai, google-cloud-{storage,bigquery,pubsub,firestore}, fastapi, uvicorn, python-dotenv, pydantic, pillow |
| Frontend | streamlit, requests                                                                                                                        |
| Test     | pytest, pytest-cov, httpx                                                                                                                  |

`httpx` is required by `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` — without it the EPIC-08 route tests cannot run at all.

## Test cases

| Test                                | Asserts                                               |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_required_packages_importable` | Every package named in the manifest imports           |
| Environment doctor check            | `doctor.py` reports "python packages installed" green |

The doctor already performs this check against a fixed list; keep that list in step with the manifest.

## Definition of done

A fresh `python -m venv venv && pip install -r requirements.txt` succeeds, and `doctor.py` reports the package check green.

## Notes

Splitting this into `requirements-dev.txt` would be conventional for a long-lived service. For a hackathon build where the same machine runs the app, the tests, and the demo, one file removes a class of "works on my machine" problems. Revisit if the project outlives the competition.
